Do NOT sweep anything in this gate.

g2-implement.title: Sweep the corpus and the tracked overlay, and invert the mandate: implement
g2-implement.imperative: THREE HALVES OF ONE GATE -- (a) and (b) because doing either alone leaves the suite red, and (c) because it is the only proof in this plan that a wrong pattern would fail. (a) SWEEP: remove all 13 'CLI fallback' clauses and all 10 agent-facing '<engine>' occurrences from skills/** (NOT skills/workbench/**, which lane D2 owns and deletes outright), AND the same text from the tracked .agent-work/templates/ overlay and its .baseline/ mirrors -- 7 '<engine>' plus 2 clauses on each side, measured. The overlay is what an agent in THIS repo actually instantiates, and the launch order's own acceptance test is to instantiate a fresh spine and read its imperatives, so a skills/-only sweep does not close #559. NOTE the occurrence/line trap: COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json tasks.archive.imperative carries TWO '<engine>' tokens on ONE line; edit both. For the 10 bound-spine clauses, replace with wording naming the real agent path -- a dispatched crew is launched with its spine bound (run_crew.py --backend cli --spine); the Agent-tool path binds nothing and is refused (#432) -- rather than deleting a sentence and leaving a reader with no answer. For the 3 second-checklist clauses (skills/interrogator/SKILL.md, skills/write-a-skill/templates/gated-engine-SKILL.template.md, skills/write-a-skill/templates/survey-SKILL.template.md) the door PROVABLY cannot reach the path -- measured: it refuses to rebind while the agent holds its own lease, 'one door drives one spine at a time', and releasing the lease to escape that fails the archive provenance check. Confirmed independently three times: lanes F and H each drove their execute.json under a hand-supplied CLI session id, and lane E's implementer drove its IMPLEMENTER_PLAN.json the same way. Reword those three to state that measured truth so no 'fallback' framing survives and no agent is stranded -- 'CLI fallback' is the wrong word because a fallback implies a working primary, and there is no primary here. (b) INVERT THE MANDATE: tests/test_mcp_adoption.py currently REQUIRES the text, across a measured NINE assertions at lines 737, 784, 834, 950, 954, 1132, 1149, 1324 and 1345 -- that is why #559's text regrew twice, and it is the mechanism, not the symptom. Turn each CLI-presence assertion into an absence assertion, generalizing the precedent ALREADY IN TREE at line 838 (TestTier2SpineAlreadyBoundForDispatchedCrews, which asserts absence for 2 files and pins the same human ruling verbatim). Where the target is a lane-D2 file (rows 950, 954, 1324, and the skills/workbench/SKILL.md entry in TIER2_SKILL_FILES) DELETE the mandate rather than inverting it: those files still carry the text, lane D2 has not merged, and an inverted assertion would go red on a file this lane is fenced from -- coverage is not lost, because the guard already asserts absence over the whole corpus. Keep every door-tool-named-affirmatively half exactly as strict. Then regenerate tests/data/store_mentions.approved.txt. (c) THE SPECIFICITY PROOF: reintroduce a genuine fallback clause AT ONE OF THE 3 REWORDED SITES and show the guard goes RED naming that site; revert, and show the reworded text itself stays GREEN. The reworded text and a reintroduction live in the same file saying nearly the same thing, so only a correct pattern passes both. Paste both runs verbatim and confirm a clean tree after the revert.

g1b-implement.imperative: The g1 reviewer found a real regrowth route the guard misses, and measured a whole surface no walk reads. Close both BEFORE the sweep, so the widened guard is still the specification the sweep is written against. (a) PLACEHOLDER-AGNOSTIC COMMAND LINES. A spine-template command line NEVER contains the literal 'checklist_engine.py' -- a placeholder stands in for it -- so the entire 'engine command line inside a JSON spine template' class currently rests on one 8-character literal, '<engine>'. Verified misses: '<cli> claim --session-id <commander-session-id>', 'If the door is down: <engine-cli> advance g1 --why ...', 'Fallback command line: {{engine}} release --session-id <work-id>'. And scripts/init_work_area.py:24 documents '<engine>' beside '<date>', '<N>', '<path>' as generic prose placeholders the resolver never touches, so a future author has no reason to reuse that exact token. Generalize the pattern from the TOKEN to the SHAPE: a placeholder-ish stand-in (angle-bracketed, brace-templated, or a shell variable) immediately followed by an engine verb, optionally followed by a flag. Pin every one of the three verified misses in TestTheInvocationPredicateItself (or a sibling), in the assertion path, so a later narrowing cannot quietly reopen the route. (b) THE TRACKED TEMPLATE OVERLAY. .agent-work/templates/ is a TRACKED overlay of the skills templates, and workbench doctrine tells an agent to PREFER it over the bundled skills/ copy when instantiating -- so after a skills/-only sweep the guard goes green while the copy an agent in THIS repo actually instantiates still hands over the second path. Extend the walk to it by a SUFFIX/DIRECTORY RULE, never a file list, and confirm no lane-D2 file enters the walk (measured: every .baseline/constellation-workbench/* file is clean). DO NOT SWEEP ANYTHING; g2 sweeps. The guard must remain RED, and its RED must now name overlay sites too.

The hook's sanctioned escapes -- block and waive -- both write to the parent's spine, so the prescribed honest stop is itself the destructive act. Sixth reproduction in this lane across three gates and both roles; the lane-H precedent the launch order warned about is not one agent's accident, it is what the hook instructs. Staged with priority; hook code and run_crew.py are outside this lane.

amendments.reason: The g1 review returned two things the frozen plan did not account for, both measured rather than argued. (1) A regrowth route the guard misses: a spine-template command line never contains the literal checklist_engine.py -- a placeholder stands in for it -- so the whole 'engine command line in a JSON template' class rested on the single token '<engine>', and '<cli>', '<engine-cli>' and '{{engine}}' all walk through clean. The reviewer verified all three. (2) A surface no walk reads: .agent-work/templates/ is a TRACKED overlay of the skills templates that workbench doctrine tells agents to PREFER when instantiating, and it carries 7 <engine> tokens and 2 CLI fallback clauses (mirrored again under .baseline/). The launch order's own acceptance test is to instantiate a fresh spine and read its imperatives, so a skills/-only sweep does not close #559. New gate g1b widens the guard for both BEFORE the sweep, keeping the guard as the specification the sweep is written against; g2 is rescoped to sweep the overlay too. Separately, g3-integrate and g4-integrate carried a check that could not pass: both required the whole-corpus guard green, but the guard walks skills/workbench/**, which lane D2 owns, deletes, and has not merged. That is the cold critic's F5 surviving into the revision at two gates it did not name. Both are rescoped to assert no violation outside skills/workbench/ -- still falsifiable, verified failing on today's dirty tree naming 10 real sites -- and g5-final keeps the unfiltered whole-corpus run on the rebased tree, which is where that assertion becomes honest.

amendments.reason: Every command postcondition in this plan opened with 'set -o pipefail;' and therefore could not pass. The engine runs a command check through _find_posix_shell(), which on POSIX returns shutil.which('sh'); /bin/sh on this host is dash, and dash rejects that option outright: '/bin/sh: 1: set: Illegal option -o pipefail', exit 2 -- before the check's own logic runs. Found by the g1b implementer when the engine refused its advance on a shell-dialect error rather than on the guard, and reproduced by me directly against /bin/sh. The provenance is worth recording: the cold plan critic correctly killed 'python3 -m pytest ... | tail -5' as a check that cannot FAIL, and offered 'drop the pipe, or prefix set -o pipefail' as the repair; the plan took the second branch, and it turned five checks that could not fail into five that could not pass. The option was inert anyway -- none of these five checks contains a pipeline whose non-final stage can fail, because the two that do pipe (g3/g4) rely on the LAST command's exit status by design. Corrected to POSIX form and re-verified in dash in all three directions: fails on today's dirty tree naming 10 real sites, passes on a workbench-only site list, passes on an empty log.
